subject: convoyHauler
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: armoured convoy hauler guarding a sealed cargo pod.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk.
reasoning:
I'm keeping the scope manageable while designing a compact armoured convoy hauler: a 6-wheeled tractor cab with armour plates, a turret, a cargo pod on a trailer bed, glowing neon strips, and a light bar, static and facing +Z, roughly 9m long, 2.8m wide, and 3.2m tall.

Since this can stay static, I don't need joints — I'll build wheels, axles, and chassis frame from boxes and cylinders, rotating cylinders to act as wheel axes, and I'm planning out the import structure using glow and panelled/metal paint kits for a layered cyberpunk look. Now I'm laying out the chassis dimensions along the z-axis: three wheel axles, a chassis frame box, and the front cab body positioned forward with defined width and height.

For the cab I'm extruding a side profile shape along the x-axis to create a sloped hood with a tilted windscreen, calculating the angled slope coordinates so a glowing cyan visor plane can sit flush against the surface facing forward and up.

Now I'm moving to the front end, planning a bull bar/ram plate wedge shape extruded at the front of the vehicle.

Adding a hazard-striped bumper decal, side armor skirts, and glowing magenta neon strips along the chassis, while checking that wheel placement doesn't clip into the cab sides given their widths.

Now I'm raising the cab base to y=1.25 to fix the overlap, then recalculating all dependent heights—slope center, headlights, bumper, wheel top, and chassis bounds—to keep everything proportioned for a bulky armored truck. I'm defining the cab's cross-section profile as a series of (z,y) coordinate points.

Still working out the polygon vertices...

Now I'm adding the cab's side window planes, then placing a roof-mounted turret with a cylindrical base, boxy head, twin barrels with glowing muzzles, plus a sensor mast and amber/magenta light bar details on the cab roof.

Adjusting the light bar position and turret placement relative to the roof edge, then adding twin exhaust stack cylinders behind the cab before moving on to the trailer bed and chassis rails.

For the sealed cargo pod, I'm using a low-poly octagonal lathe shape along the vertical axis, tapering the radius profile from the center outward to form a rounded capsule, sized to fit within the bed width.

Giving it a dark cyberpunk teal-gray paint job with hazard bands made from thin octagonal cylinder rings positioned at intervals along the pod, then adding a glowing magenta seam strip and a "SEALED" decal/emblem on the side for visual detail.

Now adding lock clamps with red glow lights on top, cradle blocks beneath the pod, rear bumper with glowing tail lights and armour guards, plus angled side shield panels in groups of four per side with gaps and neon strips underneath for that layered armored look.

I'm also planning a small sentry turret on top of the rear pod, then detailing the wheels with dark cylinders, steel hub caps, and thin magenta glow rings around the rim edges.

Now I'm positioning six wheels along the chassis and adding fenders above the rear wheels as boxes to cover them, plus side fenders up front. For paint, I'm defining the armor material with a dark gunmetal tone and weathering effects.

Weathering should accumulate as mud near the bottom edges, blending base color with noise and a muddy tan using a paint mixing function, then applying a panelled texture with rivets and dark seams from the clockwork kit's helper functions. I'm planning around six decal textures — hazard stripes, a visor, side windows, an emblem pod label, tail lights, and a license plate reading "CV-77" plus some graffiti-style text — with a glow effect layered onto the textured parts, starting with the visor.

Now I'm designing helper functions for building the model: a box helper that places geometry with color and position options (since this static model has no joints/bones to attach to), and a plane helper for texture mapping with direction and axis controls for things like side panels and the angled visor. For the pod emblem, I'm working out how to decal onto the curved octagonal lathe surface by projecting the texture at an angle onto the pod part rather than relying on uncertain flat-face positions.

I'm settling on a cyberpunk color scheme for the pod -- graphite body with a teal sheen on top and magenta glow accents, using countershading (darker on bottom, lighter on top) plus grime near the base, then wrapping it in a paneled material with rivets and seams for texture detail.

Now I'm working out the pod's placement and dimensions along the z-axis relative to the cab, exhaust stacks, and rear wheels, adjusting the chassis length and fender positions so everything fits without clipping.

Positioning the ring bands along the pod's axis, spacing them at roughly -1.3, 0, and 1.3 to keep the radius consistent across the surface.

Adding a thin glow ring near the center plus a decal placeholder for an emblem, then moving up to the pod's spine where I'm placing dark clamp boxes and small red light accents, and sketching out side armor shields near the cab.

Now I'm placing side skirt panels between the axles and figuring out where to tuck in cylindrical fuel tanks or battery packs beneath the chassis, positioning them just outside the main body width.

I'm also adding glowing magenta accent strips along the cab's lower sides as thin boxes, positioning them to run along the cab's back edge where it meets the chassis.

Now I'm working out the underchassis: a dark central chassis box running the vehicle's length, cylindrical axle bars at the wheel positions, and a front ram/bumper plate with a hazard-texture plane mounted on its forward face.

Adding brush guard details now -- vertical rods in front of the grille between the bumper top and headlight height, plus considering a glowing cyan slit for the grille texture tucked between the rods and cab front.

Working out the hood and cab geometry: front face spans y 1.55-2.15, with the nose sloping up from there to the hood edge and up to the windshield base, placing headlights around y 2.0 and the grille lower at y 1.85.

Now I'm adding small glowing wing mirrors on arms at the cab sides, then building the turret - a base cylinder on the roof near the back, a boxy turret head above it, and two gun barrels extending forward from the turret.

For the lightbar, I'm placing it lower on the roof so the guns clear above it, made from six alternating red/blue glow segments across its width. I'm adding a small cyan sensor lens on the turret front, and an antenna rod on the rear with a glowing red tip, keeping the overall height reasonable.

Now I'm adding the rear bumper and tail lights as a glowing red strip plane, plus a small license plate reading "CV-77" below it, checking the sizes don't overlap awkwardly. I'm also placing mud flaps behind the rear wheels, positioning them just clear of the rear bumper.

For decals, I'm adding a cab door plane with "CV-77 / HAULER" or "ESCORT" text and stripes, plus a cargo pod side label with a hazard triangle and "SEALED / CARGO-9 / BIO-HAZ" text, mirroring both sides so the text reads correctly from either direction.

Now I'm setting up helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and glowing neon strips to streamline building the remaining geometry while keeping the color count manageable.

Checking whether the builder needs joints for a static model—it seems joints can be omitted entirely, and painted parts can't glow while flat-colored ones can, so I'll keep neon elements unpainted. Working out the wheel loop next, placing tires at each axle with dark flat-colored rubber material.

Still writing wheel geometry...

Now I'm working out fenders over the rear axles, merging the two into one longer fender with an outer lip, and adding small amber marker lights at the front edge. I'm also starting to set up a hazard stripe texture for later use.

Designing the visor, window, taillight, plate, and emblem SVGs with their glow effects and distinct color schemes for each panel.

Now I'm building the base armor paint function with weathered mud-tone variation using noise-based mixing.

I'm defining paneled armor and pod paint variants, giving the pod a brighter off-white sealed look with grime contrast against the dark truck, and thinking about adding an accent stripe to the cab paint for visual pop.

Adding stripe logic...

With no joints defined, the lathe geometry should still work fine statically. I'm shaping the pod using a lathe outline with points swept around the axis, oriented so the front faces +z, and checking that the pod sits above the chassis top with room for cradles between them.

I'm skipping the octagon spin adjustment since the circumscribed radius is unclear, but confirming the pod's top sits around y=3.55. For the glow strip near the octagon top, I'm checking whether it lines up flush with a vertex-top or flat-top orientation, since the exact height differs slightly (3.55 vs 3.46) and could cause minor z-fighting either way.

Going with y=3.54 and a strip height of .08 so it's visibly above the surface regardless of orientation. I'm also placing iron clamps with glowing red tops at two z-positions, and working out ring radii for the bands around the pod—sizing them a bit larger (around 1.22-1.26) to avoid clipping into the pod's vertices given the uncertain 8-sided alignment.

For the cradles supporting the pod, I'm using wide iron boxes positioned to sit just under the pod's curved base, sized so only their sides peek out visibly. I'm estimating the total part count is manageable, around 150, and considering whether to add a small glowing seal detail near the rear hatch where the pod tapers.

Now I'm working out tilt angles for the side armor plates, figuring out which rotation direction makes the tops lean outward versus inward, and placing them symmetrically on both sides near the pod's shoulder height.

I'm checking clearances for the fuel tanks, neon strip, and wheel axles to make sure everything fits without overlapping, then I'll move on to writing the full build code with mirrors and other small details.

Setting up the glow and panel kit imports, deciding against using rng for random decals, and positioning the visor plane with its tilt and size relative to the cab width before extruding the cab outline...

I'm working out side window placement on the cab walls, aligning them with the beveled side faces, and now figuring out where to place the door number plate so it doesn't overlap the window region.

Writing headlight and bumper code...
